newsitem.title: USA: Meyer reportedly stresses Fed's preemptive stance.
newsitem.headline: Meyer reportedly stresses Fed's preemptive stance.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer told St. Louis businessmen on Friday that the central bank was prepared to take preemptive action if needed to keep inflation down, people who attended the meeting said.
Meyer's speech, to the St. Louis Regional Commerce and Growth Association, mostly echoed and elaborated on comments made earlier this week by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan.

As Greenspan did, Meyer made clear that the Fed is paying particular attention to developments in labor markets, including signs that worker insecurity may be abating and that wage increases may be picking up.

People who attended the meeting reported that Meyer said that the "new" part of the Fed's message was its increased willingness to take preemptive action against inflation, rather than waiting until inflation emerges.

Greenspan told the Senate Banking Committee much the same thing on Wednesday. "We cannot rule out a situation in which a preemptive policy tightening may become appropriate before any sign of actual higher inflation becomes evident," he said.
